tables.name: product_signups
tables.purpose: Records each customer's request to be notified when a specific product variant returns to stock, and tracks whether the notification was delivered.

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: Shopify numeric variant ID the customer is waiting on

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: Shopify numeric product ID for admin display and filtering

columns.name: failure_reason
columns.purpose: populated when status is failed so the admin dashboard surfaces the reason inline

columns.name: resolved_at
columns.purpose: set when the signup reaches a terminal state (notified, failed, unsubscribed)

tables.name: notification_attempts
tables.purpose: Logs every email delivery attempt for a signup so the merchant can audit successes and failures and the system can prove a notification was sent at most once.

columns.name: signup_id
columns.constraints: NOT NULL REFERENCES product_signups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
columns.purpose: links this attempt to the originating signup record

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: denormalised for querying attempts by variant without joining

tables.name: restock_processing_locks
tables.purpose: Provides a per-variant advisory lock row so concurrent inventory_levels/update deliveries for the same variant do not double-send notifications; the row is claimed atomically and released when processing completes.

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: the variant being processed; one lock row per variant

widget.purpose: Return whether the current customer is already signed up for back-in-stock notification for a given product variant.
Register a customer's email address to receive a one-time notification when a specific product variant is back in stock.
Unsubscribe a customer from a back-in-stock notification for a specific product variant.

admin.purpose: Return a cursor-paginated, status-filtered list of all back-in-stock signups and their notification outcomes for the merchant dashboard.

responseShape.signups: { id: string, variant_external_id: string, product_external_id: string, customer_email: string, status: string, failure_reason: string|null, created_at: string, resolved_at: string|null }[]

handle-inventory-level-update.description: When an inventory level update fires, resolve the variant from the inventory item, check whether quantity went above zero, claim a processing lock, fetch pending signups, retrieve variant details from Shopify, and send each customer a restock notification email, recording success or failure per signup.

steps.purpose: null-defend the available quantity (R3)
skip if inventory did not rise above zero

ifTrue.purpose: record that the event was skipped due to non-positive quantity
exit early — no restock to process

steps.purpose: build the InventoryItem GID for the Shopify query (R10)
resolve the variant ID and availableForSale from the inventory item (payload only carries inventory_item_id, not variant_id)
steps.query: query GetVariantFromInventoryItem($id: ID!) { inventoryItem(id: $id) { id variant { id title availableForSale product { id title onlineStoreUrl } } } }

steps.purpose: extract the variant node from the inventory item query result
skip if variant could not be resolved (deleted or orphaned inventory item)

ifTrue.purpose: warn that variant resolution failed
ifTrue.message: inventory_levels/update: could not resolve variant from inventory item, skipping

ifTrue.purpose: exit early — cannot identify which variant restocked

steps.purpose: skip if variant is not available for sale (above-zero quantity but product unavailable)

ifTrue.purpose: record that the variant is not purchasable despite positive inventory
ifTrue.message: inventory_levels/update: variant not availableForSale, skipping notification

ifTrue.purpose: exit early — preserve notification for genuine purchasable restock

steps.purpose: parse the raw numeric variant ID from the GID (R10)
parse the raw numeric product ID from the GID (R10)
build product URL for notification email, falling back to empty string
sanitize product title for email content
sanitize variant title for email content
check whether any pending signups exist for this variant before acquiring the lock
steps.template: SELECT COUNT(*)::int AS cnt FROM product_signups WHERE variant_external_id = ${variantIdNum} AND status = 'pending'

steps.purpose: exit early if no pending signups remain for this variant

ifTrue.purpose: record that no pending signups were found (idempotency fast-exit)
ifTrue.message: inventory_levels/update: no pending signups, treating as no-op

ifTrue.purpose: exit without any external calls

steps.purpose: ensure a lock row exists for this variant (insert with status='completed' if none present; do nothing if one already exists)
steps.template: INSERT INTO restock_processing_locks (variant_external_id, status) VALUES (${variantIdNum}, 'completed') ON CONFLICT (variant_external_id) DO NOTHING

steps.purpose: atomically transition the lock from completed to processing; zero rows means another delivery is still in flight (R1)
steps.template: UPDATE restock_processing_locks SET status = 'processing', created_at = now(), completed_at = NULL WHERE variant_external_id = ${variantIdNum} AND (status = 'completed' OR (status = 'processing' AND created_at < now() - interval '30 minutes')) RETURNING id

steps.purpose: fetch all pending signups for this variant to notify
steps.template: SELECT id, customer_email FROM product_signups WHERE variant_external_id = ${variantIdNum} AND status = 'pending'

steps.purpose: send a restock notification email to each pending signup customer and record the outcome
atomically claim this signup for notification, skipping if already moved out of pending (R1, handles unsubscribe race)
steps.template: UPDATE product_signups SET status = 'notified', resolved_at = now() WHERE id = ${signupId} AND status = 'pending' RETURNING id, customer_email

steps.purpose: send email and record attempt; on failure record permanent failure reason on signup

try.purpose: deliver the back-in-stock notification to the customer

try.template: INSERT INTO notification_attempts (signup_id, variant_external_id, outcome, failure_reason, attempted_at) VALUES (${signupId}, ${variantIdNum}, 'sent', NULL, now())

catch.purpose: revert signup to failed state and record the failure reason (R4-style failure capture)
catch.template: UPDATE product_signups SET status = 'failed', failure_reason = ${reason}, resolved_at = now() WHERE id = ${signupId}
INSERT INTO notification_attempts (signup_id, variant_external_id, outcome, failure_reason, attempted_at) VALUES (${signupId}, ${variantIdNum}, 'failed_permanent', ${reason}, now())

catch.purpose: warn on per-signup email failure for ops visibility (R8)
catch.message: restock notification send failed for signup

steps.purpose: release the per-variant processing lock on completion
steps.template: UPDATE restock_processing_locks SET status = 'completed', completed_at = now() WHERE id = ${lockId}

steps.purpose: record restock processing summary (R8)

postconditions: every pending signup for the variant is either in state 'notified' or 'failed' after processing completes
exactly one notification_attempts row exists per processed signup per restock run
the restock_processing_locks row is in 'completed' state after the run finishes
signups already in 'notified', 'failed', or 'unsubscribed' state are untouched
edgeCases: available quantity is null or zero — recipe exits before any DB write or Shopify call.
variant cannot be resolved from inventory item (deleted product) — recipe logs and exits before touching signups.
variant.availableForSale is false despite positive inventory — recipe exits and preserves notifications for a genuine purchasable restock.

concurrent second webhook delivery for same variant while first is processing — sql_claim UPDATE WHERE status='completed' OR (status='processing' AND created_at < now()-30min) returns zero rows; zeroRowAction=skip exits cleanly.
a signup is unsubscribed between the bulk SELECT and the per-signup claim — the per-signup sql_claim WHERE status='pending' returns zero rows; zeroRowAction=skip skips that item without email.
email provider returns a permanent failure — try_catch.catch flips signup to 'failed', records failure_reason, inserts failed_permanent attempt row.
all pending signups are already notified — first pendingCheck returns 0; recipe exits before acquiring lock or calling Shopify.

sweep-restock-processing-locks.description: Sweep restock_processing_locks rows that have been in processing state for more than 30 minutes (stale due to mid-run crash) back to completed so future restock webhooks for the same variant can acquire the lock.

steps.purpose: mark stale processing locks as completed so they no longer block future runs
steps.template: UPDATE restock_processing_locks SET status = 'completed', completed_at = now() WHERE status = 'processing' AND created_at < now() - interval '30 minutes' RETURNING id

steps.purpose: record sweep completion for ops visibility

postconditions: no restock_processing_locks rows older than 30 minutes remain in 'processing' state
edgeCases: no stale locks present — UPDATE matches zero rows and returns cleanly.

widget-get-signup-state.description: Look up whether a customer is currently signed up for back-in-stock notification for a given product variant and return the signup status.

steps.purpose: parse variant ID to bigint-safe number
look up existing signup for this customer-variant pair
steps.template: SELECT id, status FROM product_signups WHERE customer_email = ${customerEmail} AND variant_external_id = ${variantIdNum} LIMIT 1

steps.purpose: determine whether a signup row was found
extract status or null when no signup exists
return signup state to the widget

postconditions: response reflects current DB state for the customer-variant pair at time of request
edgeCases: customer has no signup for this variant — returns {is_signed_up: false, status: null}.
customer has a previously notified or failed signup — returns the correct terminal status so the widget renders accordingly.

widget-post-signup.description: Create a pending back-in-stock signup for a customer email and product variant, enforcing one active signup per customer-variant pair.

steps.purpose: parse variant ID to bigint-safe number
parse product ID to bigint-safe number
sanitize email to remove null bytes
insert signup or do nothing on conflict (idempotent — duplicate submission is a no-op)
steps.template: INSERT INTO product_signups (variant_external_id, product_external_id, customer_email, status, created_at) VALUES (${variantIdNum}, ${productIdNum}, ${cleanEmail}, 'pending', now()) ON CONFLICT (customer_email, variant_external_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id

steps.purpose: record signup creation or no-op for observability
return success to the widget regardless of whether the row was new or already existed

postconditions: at most one product_signups row with status='pending' exists per (customer_email, variant_external_id) pair
duplicate POST requests return success without creating additional rows
edgeCases: customer already has a pending signup for the variant — ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING returns zero rows; response is still {success: true}.
customer has a previously terminal signup (notified/failed) — the existing row is not overwritten; the customer retains their terminal status and should re-register if they want a new notification.

widget-post-signup-remove.description: Mark a customer's pending signup as unsubscribed so no restock notification is sent.

steps.purpose: parse variant ID to bigint-safe number
sanitize email to remove null bytes
atomically transition the signup from pending to unsubscribed (R1); only acts if signup is still pending
steps.template: UPDATE product_signups SET status = 'unsubscribed', resolved_at = now() WHERE customer_email = ${cleanEmail} AND variant_external_id = ${variantIdNum} AND status = 'pending' RETURNING id

steps.purpose: record unsubscribe outcome for observability
return success to the widget

postconditions: the signup row is in 'unsubscribed' state with resolved_at set, or was already not pending (no change)
edgeCases: signup does not exist or is already in a terminal state — sql_claim returns zero rows; zeroRowAction=skip proceeds to response {success: true} (idempotent).
restock webhook claimed the signup between the customer clicking unsubscribe and this request arriving — claim returns zero rows; the customer will receive the email since it was already sent.

decode cursor into (created_at, id) pair or null for first page
branch on whether a status filter and cursor were supplied

platformGaps.gap: The inventory_levels/update webhook payload does not carry variant_id; it only carries inventory_item_id.
platformGaps.mitigation: The restock recipe performs a shopify.graphql query on inventoryItem(id) immediately after receiving the webhook to resolve the associated variant and product IDs before any DB work.
platformGaps.uxImplication: Each restock webhook incurs one extra Shopify Admin API call to resolve the variant; this is within Admin API rate limits but adds one round-trip latency before notifications begin.

platformGaps.gap: No Shopify batch email mutation exists; each customer notification is an individual platform.email.send call.
platformGaps.mitigation: The restock recipe iterates pending signups with continueOnError=true and calls email.send per signup, recording each outcome individually; failures do not block successful sends for other customers.
platformGaps.uxImplication: For high-volume restock events with many signups, notification delivery takes O(n) email API calls; the merchant's admin dashboard may show partial success states while the loop is still running.

platformGaps.gap: The inventory_levels/update webhook fires on every inventory change (not only zero-to-positive transitions), requiring the handler to filter by quantity and availableForSale.
platformGaps.mitigation: The recipe guards with an early-exit decision when qty <= 0 or availableForSale is false, making non-restock inventory changes a fast no-op.

emailSpec.purpose: Notify a customer that a product variant they signed up for is back in stock and ready to purchase.

starterContent.subject: {{productTitle}} is back in stock!
starterContent.body:
Great news! {{productTitle}} – {{variantTitle}} is back in stock and available to purchase.

Shop now before it sells out again →

You're receiving this email because you signed up for a back-in-stock alert. This is a one-time notification.

uxExpectations.storefront: Widget renders on the product page as a compact 'Notify me when available' form pre-filled with the customer's email if logged in; after submission it immediately switches to a confirmation state showing 'You're on the list' with an unsubscribe link. No page reload required.
uxExpectations.admin: Dashboard prioritizes scannable status columns (pending, notified, failed, unsubscribed) with one-click status filter tabs, inline failure reasons on failed rows, and a total-signups count per variant so the merchant can immediately assess notification coverage and follow up on failures.

edgeCases: A customer submits the signup form twice for the same variant — ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING ensures exactly one pending row; the second response is still {success: true} so the widget does not show an error.

A restock webhook fires while a prior run for the same variant is still processing — the sql_claim UPDATE WHERE status='completed' OR (status='processing' AND created_at < now()-30min) returns zero rows and zeroRowAction=skip exits cleanly, preventing double sends.

A product variant is deleted before the restock notification loop runs — the inventoryItem query returns a null variant node; the recipe logs a warning and exits before touching any signup rows, leaving them in 'pending' for operator review.

The email provider returns a permanent bounce for a customer address — the try_catch.catch arm flips the signup to 'failed' with the rejection reason stored in failure_reason and inserts a 'failed_permanent' attempt row; no retry is attempted.

A customer unsubscribes after the pending-signups SELECT but before their per-signup sql_claim fires — the claim's WHERE status='pending' guard returns zero rows; zeroRowAction=skip skips that item without sending an email.

The admin dashboard receives a cursor from a deleted row's position — the (created_at, id) tuple comparison simply returns the next page relative to those values; no error occurs and the result set is consistent.
